description: The initial message-bus method set the Simulation Core serves (FR-M32-01 foundation). Lifecycle methods (handshake, ping, shutdown, health) are implemented; ledger and loop methods are the contract the Simulation Core fills in during Workstreams D and E.

handshake.description: First request after spawn. Carries the protocol version both ways; either side refuses on mismatch (FR-M3-08).

shutdown.description: Polite teardown request; the sidecar exits after answering (FR-M3-02).

health.description: Richer than ping: state, uptime, in-flight loop count.

attrib/blame.description: FR-M33-02 subset (F0 Workstream C): git-native line attribution. Every line of the given paths (or all tracked files) at ref (default HEAD) mapped to (commit, author name/email, timestamp, content). Blame never lands on merge commits; renames are followed. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

attrib/diff.description: FR-M33-02 subset (F0 Workstream C): unified-diff attribution for the working tree (default), the index (staged), or a commit range (base..compare, added lines annotated with blame attribution at compare). Renames detected; untracked files reported as added. Working-tree added lines carry commit null — there is no commit yet.

attrib/symbol.description: FR-M33-02 subset (F0 Workstream C task 14): tree-sitter line→symbol mapping — the qualified enclosing function/class of a line (e.g. "PaymentController.submit"). Unregistered languages degrade to symbol/language null, never a crash; only a missing file is an error. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

attrib/classify.description: FR-M35-02 attribution aid (F0 Workstream C task 15; gaps G3): deterministic human-vs-agent heuristics over working-tree/staged/range changes — burst size, multi-line insertion rate, new-file size, observed-session cross-reference. Keystroke cadence is unavailable for agents acting via file writes and is not a signal; fs/git timestamps only. Every file is labelled observationConfidence telemetry|inferred (inferred is the floor, never presented as fact) with an auditable rationale. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

observe/sessions.description: FR-M35-03, X-29 (F0 Workstream D tasks 18-20): the external-agent session list behind the Crown. Sessions are detected by process inspection (vendor agent process names) and the observer framework fallback chain (OTel export, git trailers, SCM/PR API, filesystem inference), each carrying a vendor tag and observation confidence (FR-M35-02: direct/telemetry/inferred). Reads a cache refreshed by the session-monitor thread — this RPC NEVER waits on observer IO (NFR-29).

observe/health.description: FR-M35-08 (F0 Workstream D task 17): per-observer health for the External Agents screen and doctor — status ok|degraded, vendor release and adapter version (versioned observer adapters), and the sticky NFR-32 degradation warnings (format change -> visible warning, never silence).

doctor/run.description: FR-M30-01: run the self-diagnostic check registry (interpreter, sidecar, keychain/signing key, ledger integrity, git hooks, observer health). Subsystems that are not built yet report a clear not-installed status with remediation instead of failing.

ledger.append.description: Append one entry to the hash-chained ledger (FR-M10-01/02). The RPC acknowledges only after the entry and chain update are durably committed (FR-M10-08). Inputs/outputs are SEC-07-redacted and stored encrypted in the blob store (FR-M10-07); the entry references their ciphertext digests. Simulation Core entries set simulated (FR-M32-02).

ledger.query.description: Filterable entry stream (FR-M10-12, FR-M11-02): story, agent (actor), vendor, action type, sequence range, time range.

ledger.getEntry.description: FR-M11-03 entry detail: full prompt/context and output (decrypted when the caller's sidecar holds the subject key), tool calls, confidence, cost, chain hashes.

ledger.verify.description: FR-M11-01 chain integrity verdict: verified through sequence N, or a tamper indication naming the first divergent sequence (FR-M10-09).

ledger.proof.description: FR-M11-04 proof inspection: an inclusion proof for one entry, or a consistency proof between two tree sizes (RFC 6962/9162 shapes).

ledger.exportBundle.description: FR-M11-05/FR-M36-04/SEC-29/FR-M12-11 (F0 Workstream E task 25): the full signed audit bundle for any sequence range, date range, agent or story — entries with their exact hash preimages, Merkle inclusion proofs against the signed tree head, an Ed25519 signature over the whole bundle, and a compliance section mapping bundle fields to NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) provenance practice, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 record-keeping clauses and EU AI Act Article 12. Verifies standalone with the open reference verifier (FR-M36-06) using only the bundle's own public key.

hook/install.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 23): install the opt-in commit-msg trailer hook into the workspace repository. The hooks directory is resolved with `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, so a configured core.hooksPath is honoured. A foreign commit-msg hook is never overwritten: it is moved to commit-msg.meridian-backup and the Meridian hook chains to it (runs it first). Idempotent; one-action removal via hook/remove.

hook/status.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 23): report the commit-msg hook state — installed/foreign/chained, and where — so the UI and doctor show the same facts.

hook/remove.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 23): remove the Meridian commit-msg hook in one action, restoring a backed-up foreign hook if one was chained. Never touches a hook that is not Meridian's.

hook/pending.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 23): record a pending commit linkage — the staged-content hash (git write-tree) mapped to the ledger sequence range recorded for those changes. The commit-msg hook resolves this record at commit time and appends `Meridian-Ledger: <seq range>` to the message. Records are consumed once; a commit whose staged hash has no pending record passes through untouched.

trailers/parse.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 24): agent identity trailers. Every vendor's `Co-Authored-By` variant (Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, generic `Name <email>`) in the repository's commit messages parsed into attribution records, with `Meridian-Ledger` ranges alongside; `message` parses one raw message without git. Meridian's own `Co-Authored-By: Meridian <...>` is recognised and reserved for Meridian-authored commits (meridianAuthored). Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

loop.start.description: Start one of the six canonical loops (FR-M4-03).

loop.stop.description: Stop a running loop; the loop checkpoints first (FR-M4-05).

loop.status.description: Current state of a loop instance.

gate.evaluate.description: FR-M12-01/FR-M12-09 (F1 Workstream B task 9): evaluate a packet/PR payload against a named gate profile of the governance policy pack (FR-M12-01, fail-closed YAML). Every criterion is a machine-checkable DoR/DoD predicate (requiredFields, testEvidence, securityScan, humanApproval) with a pass/fail reason; the verdict is their conjunction. Fail-closed pack or unknown profile blocks. The decision is ledger-recorded (actionType gate) BEFORE the response returns (FR-M10-08).

gate.profiles.description: FR-M12-01 (F1 Workstream B task 9): list the gate profiles of the active governance policy pack — name, description, and the ordered criterion ids each profile checks. Fail-closed packs report their errors and an empty profile list.

gate.approve.description: FR-M12-05/FR-M12-07 (F1 Workstream B task 10): record a human approval for a merge subject (protected branch or PR id) bound to a commit digest. The approver identity comes from the identity interface (git user.name/email per D9, swappable); anonymous approval is refused, never recorded. The approval lands in the ledger (actionType approval, humanActor/humanRole set) BEFORE the RPC returns (FR-M10-08).

gate.status.description: FR-M12-05 (F1 Workstream B task 10): merge-gate status for a branch/PR subject at an optional head commit. approved only when the subject is unprotected or a recorded human approval binds the head digest; blocked carries the missing-criteria report (no approval, approval invalidated by a changed head, or an active governance halt). Read-only — decides nothing, records nothing.

steer.send.description: Governor tier stub (FR-M25-01; F1): steer a running session. Same tier-enforcement role as gate.evaluate.

trust.summary.description: Governor tier stub (FR-M37-*; F0 subset/F1 full): trust and rejection analytics summary. Same tier-enforcement role as gate.evaluate.

trust/detectRejections.description: FR-M37-01 subset (F0 Workstream F task 28): deterministic rejection capture from git history over base..ref (the attribution engine's diff/blame — zero model calls, FR-M36-07). A change is rejected when reverted (a later commit removes its added lines and restores its removed lines), force-amended away (its commit is unreachable and its content no longer exists at ref), or replaced within windowDays (default 7 — the meridian.rejectionWindowDays workspace setting). Each detected rejection is recorded in the ledger as an entry with actionType "rejection" carrying the rejected entry's sequence (from the commit's Meridian-Ledger trailer when present), the rejecting commit and the reason; re-running is idempotent (duplicates are skipped, never double-recorded). Detection records facts — no gate exists and none is implied.

trust/classify.description: FR-M37-06 (F0 Workstream F task 29): greenfield/brownfield classification of a story's or session's changes (a commit list or base..compare range). Greenfield when the new-file ratio is >= newFileRatioThreshold (default 0.5 — meridian.greenfieldNewFileRatio) OR the median age of the touched code is < maxMedianAgeDays (default 30 — meridian.greenfieldMaxMedianAgeDays). Deterministic from git; zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

trust/rejectionRate.description: FR-M17-05 + FR-M37-01 (F0 Workstream F task 30): rejection rate per agent, per repository, split greenfield/brownfield (G6), derived from the ledger on demand — proposed changes are ledger entries with actionType "diff", rejections are the entries they link to via a rejection entry's rejectedSequence. No separate metrics database: the numbers recompute from ledger entries and cache in-process, invalidated on append. Stories are classified via trust/classify when storyCommits (storyId -> commits) and repoPath are provided; stories without commit data are reported in the unclassified bucket, never silently dropped.

acp/sessionBegin.description: FR-M34-01/02 (F1 Workstream A task 4): the extension host ACP client reports a hosted agent session starting; the sidecar records a `session_begin` ledger entry (actorKind external, vendor acp, direct confidence) before the agent's first turn.

acp/sessionEnd.description: FR-M34-01/02 (F1 Workstream A task 4): the extension host reports a hosted session ending (stop reason, timing); the sidecar records a `session_end` ledger entry, attributing it to the same actor as the session's begin entry.

acp/permissionDecision.description: FR-M34-04/SEC-28 (F1 Workstream A task 4): records one ACP permission decision — selected option, cancellation, policy denial (outcome denied_by_policy, reason cited) or a SEC-28 re-request auto-denial — as a `permission_decision` ledger entry so the governance trail is durable before and independently of the human answer.

worktree/create.description: FR-M18-01/02/05/07 (F1 Workstream A task 5): create the story worktree for a hosted agent — a linked git worktree under <repo>/.meridian/worktrees/<story-id>/ on branch meridian/<story-id> (configurable via baseBranch) forked from the base branch, with a worktree-local agent git identity derived from the adapter id and a worktree-local commit-msg hook appending the Meridian-Hosted-Agent trailer to every commit the agent makes. The primary working tree is NEVER the write target. Ledger-recorded (action_type worktree_create, worktree_ref set).

worktree/list.description: FR-M18-01 (F1 Workstream A task 5): the Meridian-managed story worktrees of this repository (those under .meridian/worktrees/), each with branch, base and head. Read-only; consumed by the open-in-window command (FR-M18-08) among others.

worktree/remove.description: FR-M18-01 (F1 Workstream A task 5): remove a story worktree (git worktree remove; refuses when the worktree is dirty unless force). The branch is NOT deleted here — that is story abort (worktree/abortStory) or post-merge GC (FR-M18-09). Ledger-recorded (action_type worktree_remove, worktree_ref set).

worktree/abortStory.description: FR-M18-04 (F1 Workstream A task 5): story abort — remove the story worktree, delete the story branch when it has never been pushed (a pushed branch is kept and branchKeptReason says why), and ledger-record the abort (action_type story_abort, worktree_ref set). The primary working tree is left byte-identical (AC-14).

worktree/conflicts.description: FR-M18-03 (F1 Workstream A task 5, AC-13): pre-flight conflict detection before a packet starts — divergence between the story branch and the base branch (unmerged upstream changes), uncommitted changes in the primary tree colliding with the packet's target paths (all dirty files reported when targetPaths is absent), and uncommitted/unpushed state in the story worktree itself. Returns a structured report; blocked=true means the run must not start. The RunRequest/preflight flow (M40, gaps_initiation §7.11) consumes this report.

mcp/invoke.description: FR-M34-06 (F1 Workstream A task 6): the MCP server gateway. The standalone MCP server process (extension/src/mcp/, governor tier) forwards every MCP tools/call as one mcp/invoke; the sidecar's tier gate is the permission gate (governor disabled => TIER_DISABLED, G5), the call is ledger-recorded as a `tool_call` entry (vendor mcp, direct confidence) BEFORE it runs, and the named tool maps onto the existing read-only handler — ledger_query -> ledger.query, ledger_export_bundle -> ledger.exportBundle, ledger_verify -> ledger.verify, trust_rejection_rate -> trust/rejectionRate. Unknown tool names are refused with INVALID_PARAMS listing the available tools; the underlying result passes through verbatim.

tiers/set.description: FR-M36-05: notification carrying the enabled tier set after a meridian.tiers configuration change, so a tier flip needs no reinstall and no window reload. The base tier (flight-recorder) is always enabled regardless of payload.

$/cancel.description: Notification cancelling an in-flight request by id (FR-M1-09).

protocolVersion.description: Must equal PROTOCOL_VERSION or the sidecar refuses with PROTOCOL_MISMATCH.

tiers.description: FR-M36-05: tiers enabled in this workspace (from the meridian.tiers setting). Absent means the sidecar default: flight-recorder only. The base tier is always enabled regardless.

workspaceDir.description: Absolute workspace path. The ledger lives at <workspaceDir>/.meridian/ledger (FR-M10-01). Absent: ledger RPCs answer LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE until configured.

ledgerSigningKey.description: Base64-encoded 32-byte Ed25519 seed (FR-M10-04), sourced from the extension host's OS-keychain-backed SecretStorage (SEC-06) and provisioned over this handshake. Held in memory only; never persisted to disk or written into the ledger. Absent: the sidecar signs tree heads with an ephemeral key and doctor reports the missing keychain key.

DoctorCheckStatus.description: Outcome of one doctor check. warn means usable but degraded or not yet installed; fail means broken and actionable.

id.description: Stable machine id, e.g. interpreter, sidecar, ledger.

detail.description: What was found, in one line.

remediation.description: Actionable fix; always present on warn and fail.

checks.description: Subset of check ids to run; absent runs the whole registry.

workspaceDir.description: Absolute path of the workspace folder; the git-hooks check needs it.

status.description: Worst status across all checks: fail > warn > pass.

repoPath.description: Absolute path of the git repository (any directory inside it is accepted and resolved to the toplevel).

paths.description: Worktree-relative file filter; absent blames every tracked file.

line.description: 1-based line number in the ref's version of the file.

commit.description: Full hex sha of the introducing commit; never a merge commit.

content.description: Line content without the terminator (CRLF tolerated).

repoPath.description: Absolute path of the git repository (any directory inside it is accepted and resolved to the toplevel).

base.description: Range start (commit-ish). With compare: base..compare; alone: base vs worktree.

compare.description: Range end (commit-ish); added lines are blame-annotated at this ref.

staged.description: Diff the index against HEAD (base optionally overrides HEAD).

oldLine.description: 1-based in the base version; null for pure additions.

newLine.description: 1-based in the compare version; null for removals.

commit.description: Introducing commit for range-diff added lines (blame at compare); null for worktree/index changes.

repoPath.description: Absolute path of the git repository (any directory inside it is accepted and resolved to the toplevel).

language.description: Registered language id; null when the extension is not registered.

symbol.description: Qualified enclosing definition, e.g. PaymentController.submit; null when none or degraded.

AttribObservedSession.description: An externally observed agent session (Workstream D supplies these; the heuristic only consumes them). Its presence covering an edit window raises the agent attribution weight and lifts the label to telemetry.

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 or epoch seconds; absent means currently active. A file edited before this time is not covered.

AttribAttribution.description: agent | human | mixed | unknown. unknown is a first-class honest answer when no signal fires (G3).

burstLines.description: Lines added in the same timestamp sweep / commit as this file's edits.

multiLineInsertRate.description: Fraction of insertion hunks adding >=5 lines at once.

editTimestamp.description: Filesystem mtime of the edited file, ISO 8601 UTC; null for deletes.

observationConfidence.description: FR-M35-02; heuristic output is never better than telemetry and the floor is inferred.

rationale.description: Human-readable signals behind the weight, for UI disclosure.

LedgerAppendParams.description: One ledger entry, §7.2 columns in camelCase. input/output are redacted (SEC-07), encrypted and content-addressed (FR-M10-07); blob_subject selects the per-subject key (FR-M10-14).

input.description: Full prompt/context; redacted + encrypted into the blob store.

output.description: Resulting output; redacted + encrypted into the blob store.

vendor.description: Default 'meridian'; external agents carry their vendor (FR-M35-03).

origin.description: FR-M40-02: written with the run's first entry.

simulated.description: FR-M32-02 simulation marker; absent means false.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC override (replay/golden corpus); absent = now.

blobSubject.description: Subject for the per-subject blob key; default 'default'.

hash.description: entry_hash hex, chained from the previous (FR-M10-02).

treeHead.description: Present when this append emitted a signed tree head (FR-M10-04).

TreeHead.description: FR-M10-04 signed tree head: the Merkle root over entries 1..seq, Ed25519-signed; hex-encoded.

LedgerEntry.description: FR-M11-02 stream shape: one ledger entry with chain hashes; blob payloads are referenced by digest/ref, not inlined.

toolCallsSummary.description: Count of tool calls; the array itself is in the entry detail (FR-M11-03).

rejectedSequence.description: FR-M37-01: on actionType "rejection" entries — the rejected entry's ledger sequence.

rejectedCommit.description: FR-M37-01: on rejection entries — the commit whose change was rejected.

rejectingCommit.description: FR-M37-01: on rejection entries — the commit that rejected it (null for force_amended).

LedgerGetEntryResult.description: FR-M11-03 detail. input/output carry the decrypted blob text when the sidecar holds the subject key; *Available flags say whether decryption succeeded (false when the key was crypto-shredded).

upTo.description: Verify a prefix only; absent verifies the whole chain.

LedgerInclusionProof.description: RFC 6962 audit path for one leaf; hex-encoded hashes, leaf-upwards order (verifier: RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2).

LedgerConsistencyProof.description: RFC 6962/9162 consistency proof between two tree sizes; hex-encoded hashes (verifier: RFC 9162 §2.1.4.2).

fromSize.description: Consistency proof: the earlier tree size.

toSize.description: Consistency proof: the later tree size.

fromTimestamp.description: ISO-8601 lower bound on entry timestamps (with the sequence range).

toTimestamp.description: ISO-8601 upper bound on entry timestamps (with the sequence range).

LedgerBundleEntry.description: One entry in an audit bundle: the FR-M11-02 stream shape plus ciphertext refs and digests, so a third-party verifier can check the chain segment without any key. `hashPayload` is the exact JSON-native preimage of the entry hash (ledger columns minus entryHash/previousHash, digests hex-projected) — the open verifier hashes it byte-for-byte per the canonical JSON rules; it is the anchor of truth, the sibling fields are the human-readable view.

hashPayload.description: The exact preimage of entryHash per the open ledger spec: ledger_entry columns minus entryHash/previousHash, byte digests hex-projected, JSON-native values.

publicKey.description: Base64 raw public key; signature verification needs no trust in Meridian servers (SEC-29).

LedgerBundleInclusion.description: RFC 6962 §2.1.1 audit path proving one entry's leaf (its entryHash) is included in the Merkle tree the signed tree head commits to.

sequence.description: The ledger sequence this proof is for (1-based; the leaf index is sequence - 1).

LedgerBundleProofs.description: Merkle proofs for every included entry, against the tree size and root the signed tree head commits to (FR-M36-04/SEC-29: the bundle verifies standalone).

LedgerBundleSignature.description: Ed25519 signature over the whole bundle (FR-M36-04): `digest` is SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the entire bundle object minus this signature block; the signature signs the 32 digest bytes with the ledger key. Verification needs only the bundled public key (SEC-29).

digest.description: Hex SHA-256 of the canonical bundle core (bundle minus this block).

signature.description: Hex Ed25519 signature over the raw 32 digest bytes.

LedgerComplianceMapping.description: One mapping from a bundle field set to a record-keeping requirement (FR-M12-11 as amended by gaps-requirements M12: NIST SSDF AI provenance + ISO/IEC 42001 + EU AI Act Article 12).

LedgerComplianceSection.description: The compliance section: which standards the bundle maps to and every field-level mapping (FR-M36-04, FR-M12-11).

formatVersion.description: Bundle format v1; pinned by the open ledger spec (FR-M36-06, docs/open-ledger-spec/).

treeHead.description: Signed head covering the ledger tip at export time; absent only when the ledger has no entries yet.

workspaceDir.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

chained.description: True when a foreign commit-msg hook was backed up and is invoked by the Meridian hook before its own trailer logic.

alreadyInstalled.description: True when the hook was already Meridian's — install is idempotent.

installed.description: A commit-msg hook exists and carries the Meridian marker.

foreignHook.description: A commit-msg hook exists that is NOT Meridian's — it is left untouched.

removed.description: False when there was no Meridian hook to remove; the repository is left untouched.

restoredBackup.description: True when a chained foreign hook was restored to commit-msg.

stagedHash.description: The staged-content key: the hex of the tree object git write-tree produces for the index (`git write-tree`).

TrailerAttribution.description: One Co-Authored-By trailer value as an attribution record (FR-M36-03, task 24): the claimed identity, the vendor it resolves to (claude | github-copilot | cursor | generic | meridian | unknown), and whether this is Meridian's own reserved co-author line.

TrailerCommit.description: One commit's trailer facts: its agent attributions and the Meridian-Ledger sequence ranges it carries. `commit`/`authoredAt` are null only for the direct-message parse path.

repoPath.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

ref.description: Range or rev to walk, default HEAD. Any git log ref grammar (e.g. a..b).

since.description: ISO-8601 cutoff; only commits at or after it are parsed.

message.description: Parse this raw commit message directly — no repository needed; returns a single synthetic commit.

lastCheckpoint.description: Durable checkpoint id (FR-M4-05), present once the loop has checkpointed.

gate.description: Gate profile name from the policy pack (FR-M12-01), e.g. ready, verify, security, review.

packet.description: The packet/PR payload the criteria check: fields (storyId, branch, headCommit...), evidence artifacts (kind/status/criticalFindings), approvals. Free-form; criteria address it by key.

policyPath.description: Optional explicit policy pack path; defaults to the workspace override then the repository policy directory.

policyVersion.description: governance/v<N> of the pack that decided; governance/invalid on a fail-closed pack.

failClosed.description: True when the active pack failed closed (malformed/missing policy) — every evaluation blocks.

reasons.description: One reason per failed criterion (plus policy errors when fail-closed).

criteria.description: Ordered criterion ids the profile checks.

subject.description: The merge subject: protected branch name or PR id.

commit.description: Head commit digest the approval binds. A changed head invalidates the approval.

role.description: The approver's role (humanRole in the ledger; FR-M20 lands role checks in workstream C).

sequence.description: Ledger sequence of the approval entry — durable before this response returns.

commit.description: Current head digest; an approval bound to a different digest is invalidated.

requiredApproval.description: True when the subject is a protected branch.

halted.description: True when an active governance halt blocks this subject.

approvalSequence.description: The bound approval's ledger sequence; present only when approved via an approval.

repoPath.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

base.description: Optional commit-ish; detection covers base..ref. Absent: the whole ref history.

windowDays.description: The replaced-within-window bound in days (default 7 — meridian.rejectionWindowDays).

repoId.description: Repository identifier written to the rejection entries' repo_id column (default: the repository folder name).

storyId.description: Fallback story id for rejection entries whose rejected commit carries no resolvable Meridian-Ledger trailer.

actorId.description: Fallback actor id (default "unknown") for the same case.

rejectingCommit.description: The commit that rejected the change; null for force_amended (the change vanished with the amend).

rejectedAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC of the rejecting commit (the rejected commit's date for force_amended).

rejectedSequence.description: The rejected ledger entry's sequence, from the commit's Meridian-Ledger trailer when present.

recordedSequence.description: The ledger sequence of the rejection entry that was (or already had been) appended.

alreadyRecorded.description: True when a rejection entry for this rejectedCommit/rejectingCommit/reason/repoId already existed — detection is idempotent.

recorded.description: Rejection entries appended to the ledger in this call.

duplicatesSkipped.description: Detections already present in the ledger (idempotent re-run).

repoPath.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

commits.description: The story's/session's commits (full or abbreviated shas). Takes precedence over base/compare.

compare.description: Classify the base..compare range instead of an explicit commit list.

medianTouchedCodeAgeDays.description: Median age in days of the pre-existing code the changes touched (per-line git history age); null when the story only added files.

proposed.description: Proposed changes: ledger entries with actionType "diff" in scope.

rejected.description: Proposed changes whose sequence is carried as rejectedSequence by a rejection entry in scope.

repoPath.description: Repository for greenfield/brownfield classification. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

storyCommits.description: storyId -> the story's commits, used to classify each in-scope story (trust/classify). Stories without an entry land in the unclassified bucket.

split.description: greenfield / brownfield / unclassified buckets (G6: every trust metric reports the split).

cacheHit.description: True when served from the in-process cache (FR-M17-05: derived from the ledger, cached, invalidated on append).

ObservationConfidence.description: FR-M35-02 observation confidence: direct (the agent's own telemetry/ACP session), telemetry (evidence the agent left behind: git trailers, SCM/PR API, OS process listing), inferred (filesystem/git inference — the floor, never silence).

ObserveSessionsParams.description: SEC-27: observer-facing APIs accept NO credential parameters — the observation surface is one-way. Empty params; additionalProperties false keeps it that way.

ObserveSession.description: X-29: one external agent session as shown in the Crown — vendor tag (FR-M35-03) + observation confidence (FR-M35-02), never indistinguishable from a Meridian-native pass.

vendor.description: claude-code | copilot | cursor | codex | devin | gemini

pid.description: OS pid when detected by process inspection (X-29).

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC; null when unknown (process sessions).

warnings.description: Sticky NFR-32 degradation warnings visible in the UI.

ObserverHealth.description: FR-M35-08: one observer adapter's health — versioned against the vendor release.

status.description: degraded means an NFR-32 downgrade warning is active — observation continues at lower confidence, never silence.

monitorRunning.description: True once the X-29 session monitor thread is polling.

agentId.description: The adapter id (Meridian governance manifest id) the hosted agent runs under.

sessionId.description: The ACP session id the agent issued.

cwd.description: Workspace directory the session runs against.

policyVersion.description: Version/tag of the Meridian policy the host checked the session under (the acp-permissions policy file); absent = sidecar default.

agentId.description: The adapter id, when the host knows it; absent = the sidecar attributes the end to the begin entry's actor.

stopReason.description: The ACP stop reason that ended the last turn (end_turn, cancelled, refusal…), when known.

policyVersion.description: Policy version the session ran under, for the record.

adapterId.description: The adapter (manifest id) the permission request belongs to; the durable lookup key for SEC-28 re-request checks.

optionId.description: The permission option selected, when outcome is selected.

outcome.description: selected/cancelled record the human's answer; denied_by_policy records a pre-prompt refusal by the FR-M34-04 policy gate (allow-list, declared needs, suspension) or a SEC-28 re-request auto-denial — the human NEVER saw the prompt for those.

reason.description: Why the decision is what it is — for denied_by_policy, the citation (policy rule, prior decision) the UI and SEC-28 audits surface.

policyVersion.description: Version/tag of the acp-permissions policy that produced a denied_by_policy outcome.

recorded.description: True when the session fact was appended to the ledger.

WorktreeInfo.description: FR-M18-01/02: one Meridian-managed story worktree. `path` is absolute; `worktreeRef` the repo-relative form written to ledger worktree_ref entries.

adapterId.description: The hosted-agent adapter id the worktree-local git identity and commit trailer derive from (FR-M18-05/07).

dirty.description: True when the worktree has uncommitted or untracked changes.

unpushedCommits.description: Commits on the story branch not reachable from the base branch.

storyId.description: Story (or run) id; the worktree lives at <repo>/.meridian/worktrees/<story-id>/.

adapterId.description: The hosted agent's adapter id; the worktree-local git identity and Meridian-Hosted-Agent trailer derive deterministically from it. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._-].

repoPath.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.
Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

force.description: Remove even when the worktree is dirty (the caller asserts the content is expendable). Default false: a dirty worktree is refused with an actionable error so hosted-agent output is never silently destroyed (R14).

reason.description: Why the worktree is being removed; recorded in the ledger entry's input blob.

repoPath.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

branch.description: The story branch — still present; only worktree/abortStory deletes it.

repoPath.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

branchDeleted.description: True when the (never-pushed) story branch was deleted; false when a pushed branch was kept.

branchKeptReason.description: Present exactly when branchDeleted is false — the branch exists on a remote, so abort keeps it for the record.

WorktreeConflictKind.description: FR-M18-03: one detected conflict class. unmerged_upstream — the story branch has fallen behind the base branch; primary_uncommitted — the human has uncommitted changes in the primary tree colliding with the packet's target paths; worktree_uncommitted — the story worktree carries uncommitted state; worktree_unpushed — the story branch has commits not on the base branch (unpushed work that would be discarded).

path.description: The colliding worktree-relative file, when the conflict is file-scoped; null for branch-level conflicts.

storyId.description: The story about to run; without it, only primary-tree checks run.

baseBranch.description: The base branch to check divergence against, default main (FR-M18-02 configurable).

targetPaths.description: The files the packet targets (FR-M18-03). Absent: every dirty file in the primary tree is reported.

repoPath.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

blocked.description: True when at least one conflict was detected — the packet must not start (AC-13).

McpInvokeParams.description: One MCP tool call as forwarded by the MCP server process (FR-M34-06).

tool.description: The MCP tool name: ledger_query | ledger_export_bundle | ledger_verify | trust_rejection_rate.

arguments.description: Passthrough params for the underlying read-only method (the ledger.query / ledger.exportBundle / ledger.verify / trust-rejectionRate shapes).

client.description: Optional MCP client identification recorded as the ledger entry's actor_id (default mcp-client).

sessionId.description: Optional MCP session correlation recorded as external_session_id.

McpInvokeResult.description: The underlying handler's result, passed through verbatim under `result`.

result.description: The underlying method's result JSON, unmodified.
